title: api-gateway: tighten routing rules and increase streaming proxy buffers; enforce payload size limits for OpenAI compat
author: Anjali Menon
body: Motivation: We have observed a class of production incidents where large streaming responses combined with cross-region routing resulted in partial payload truncation or client-side stream resets. This PR addresses three related surface issues: 1) stricter routing rule evaluation to avoid accidental cross-tenant route fallthroughs under load, 2) explicit payload size limits / validation for OpenAI-compat endpoints to ensure function/tool-calling tokens are not silently dropped, and 3) increase and dynamically tune streaming proxy buffers and backpressure windows to reduce stream resets for long-running responses. Changes are backwards-compatible for consumers but tighten server-side validation to prevent silent data loss. Summary of changes: - routing: add explicit route precedence table and fast-path for pinned routes (api-gateway/routing.go, api-gateway/router_test.go) - payload limits: add OpenAI compatibility layer validation that rejects requests > 4MB payload or with too-large function call payloads (openai-compat/adapter.go) - streaming proxy: increase default read/write buffers, add adaptive buffer growth based on observed chunk latency, and add nicer observability metrics for per-connection buffer usage (api-gateway/proxy.go, observability/metrics.yaml) - tests: new unit + integration tests for function-calling boundary conditions and streaming stability under simulated high-latency links - docs: update API surface notes and migration guidance for teams relying on implicit behavior (redwood-docs/guides/api-gateway/compatibility.md) Checklist: - [x] Add routing precedence table and fast-path - [x] Add request validation for OpenAI-compat endpoints - [x] Increase proxy buffer defaults and add adaptive growth logic - [x] Add unit and integration tests covering edge cases (function-calling limits + streaming aborts) - [x] Update docs and release notes - [x] Run benchmark suite and smoke test on staging Testing and results: Unit tests: added coverage for invalid function payloads, route precedence and buffer resize events. Integration tests: run e2e streaming harness under simulated 200ms/500ms RTT; observed stream reset rate reduced from 3.2% to 0.4% and median tail latency improved by ~18% for 16k token responses in our staging cluster. CI: All checks passed after one flaky integration rerun. Rollout / migration: Feature is gated behind a runtime feature-flag (api.gateway.streaming.buffer_adaptive=true) default-enabled for hosted; Dedicated/Private customers will be rolled out via config and notified in migration notes. Breaking changes: None expected; the only user-visible behavior is earlier rejection of oversized payloads which previously could lead to undefined truncation. If you relied on implicit acceptance of >4MB OpenAI schema payloads, please update client-side validation. Related: ENG-2789 (streaming stability), ENG-2815 (openai-compat function calling regressions), SUP-4421 (customer incident that motivated limit enforcement).

review_comments: Michael Chen: Please add a unit test that exercises route fallthrough in the presence of middleware-modified headers — I want to ensure precedence is evaluated after middleware changes.
Anjali Menon: Added router_test.go case to validate middleware header mutation path and route precedence ordering.
Sonia Patel: Concern: rejecting >4MB payloads may break a few enterprise customers who send large tool descriptors; can we surface a clear error code and provide config to bump the limit?
Anjali Menon: Added clear 413 response with structured error payload and a runtime config (openai_compat.max_payload_bytes) that Dedicated/Private can increase; documented in compatibility.md.
Liam O'Connor: Confirmed that buffer growth does not cause unbounded memory usage in stress tests; left a small nits request to cap adaptive growth at 8x default.
Anjali Menon: Added adaptive cap to 8x and a metric that surfaces current cap usage; updated release notes.
ci_checks: integration-tests: pass (1 rerun due to known flaky test)
merge_outcome: Merged into main with squash; PR commit squashed as: 'api-gateway: routing precedence, streaming proxy buffer improvements, and OpenAI compat payload validation'
release_notes: API Gateway: tightened routing precedence to avoid accidental cross-tenant fallthroughs; OpenAI-compat endpoints now validate payload sizes and will return 413 for requests over default limit (4MB) — configurable via runtime; streaming proxy buffers increased and now support adaptive growth to reduce stream resets under high latency, improving long-response stability. See docs for migration guidance.
notes_for_ops: Staging rollout observed reduced stream reset rate and improved tail latency. Ops should monitor new metric 'api_gateway.connection.buffer_cap_usage' and alert on >90% sustained usage per instance. Runtime flag 'api.gateway.streaming.buffer_adaptive' can be toggled per-cluster.
changelog_entry: api-gateway: routing precedence + streaming proxy buffer tuning + openai-compat payload validation
